score_scale: Each criterion scored 1-10. Overall = weighted mean. pass_threshold applies to the geometric-median aggregate across the panel.

criteria.name: Tempo matches the idiom (opening vs ending)
criteria.anchor: Openings 130-180 BPM (J-rock often 170+); endings 70-120 BPM (Virtual Reflections CAMPAIGN.md anisong craft table; genres.yaml anime-opening notes).
criteria.evidence: measure.py bpm + bpm_candidates. Accept a candidate in range at confidence >= 0.25.
criteria.guide: 10 = in-range candidate with confidence >= 0.35. 7 = in-range at lower confidence. 4 = 5+ BPM outside. 1 = nothing in range.

criteria.name: IV-V-iii-vi 'royal road' progression (王道進行)
criteria.anchor: The IV-V-iii-vi progression is nicknamed 'the anime progression'; a 2023 Music Theory Spectrum study found it across a large share of Japan's best-selling songs for decades. Opens on the subdominant, lands on the minor vi (CAMPAIGN.md anisong craft reference).
criteria.evidence: The ABC score / chord annotation when present; otherwise the style prompt's harmony claim. Unverifiable from measurements alone — mark it so.
criteria.guide: 10 = progression present in the score/prompt verbatim. 7 = claimed, unverified. 4 = different progression claimed. 1 = no harmonic claim or contradiction.

criteria.name: FINAL CHORUS JUMPS UP ONE KEY (openings) / gentle key lift (endings)
criteria.anchor: The final-chorus modulation up ONE KEY is the genre's DEFINING gesture — in J-pop practice that is a +1 semitone (or +2 semitone) lift; omit it and the track reads as generic rock (CAMPAIGN.md; genres.yaml anime-opening notes: 'A generation without the key-changed final chorus is OUT of genre - reject it'). The final chorus typically occupies the last ~20-30% of the track and is its loudest section. Endings: gentle key lift in the final chorus; hard-cut ending is a defect — the tail fades the light (genres.yaml anime-ending notes).
criteria.evidence: ABC score modulation markers / prompt claim / RMS evidence of a final-section lift (a key-change chorus typically reads as the loudest section — rms_1s_max_db lands late).
criteria.guide: 10 = key-change claimed + late-track energy peak consistent. 7 = claimed, evidence ambiguous. 4 = no key change on an opening claim. 1 = no final-chorus lift AND flat ending energy.

criteria.name: 90-second TV-edit density (openings)
criteria.anchor: Openings are written to survive a 90-second TV edit: maximum information density, no wasted bars; dense layers — piano AND strings together, busy drums, melodic bass (CAMPAIGN.md craft table).
criteria.evidence: rms_1s_spread_db (density shifts), duration, the style prompt.
criteria.guide: 10 = dense-arrangement claim + dynamic evidence of tight section turns. 7 = claimed, partially verifiable. 4 = sparse arrangement on an opening claim. 1 = thin and wandering.

criteria.name: Japanese vocals in Japanese script
criteria.anchor: Japanese script (kana/kanji), NOT romaji. For Suno, lyrics must be written in Japanese script for correct pronunciation (CAMPAIGN.md craft table). Romaji lyrics produce wrong pronunciation; English vocals are out of idiom for the anison lane. Chorus lines typically 7-9 morae per phrase in J-pop lyric practice.
criteria.guide: 10 = lyrics in kana/kanji. 7 = mixed script with Japanese lines carrying the chorus. 4 = romaji. 1 = English-only on an anison claim.

criteria.name: Master hits the lane loudness target
criteria.guide: 10 = within +/-1 dB. 7 = within +/-3 dB. 4 = 3-6 dB off. 1 = 6+ dB off.

reject_signals: anime-opening without the key-changed final chorus — OUT of genre, reject regardless of other scores (genres.yaml is explicit)
anime-ending with a hard-cut ending — defect, the tail fades the light
English-only lyrics on an anison claim
tempo outside the idiom range with no in-range candidate
